Using $\cos^2 A - \cos^2 B = \tfrac{\cos 2A - \cos 2B}{2}$:

$$\cos^2\tfrac{x}{2} - \cos^2\tfrac{(2r+1)x}{2} = \tfrac{\cos x - \cos((2r+1)x)}{2}$$

Applying $\cos A - \cos B = -2\sin\tfrac{A+B}{2}\sin\tfrac{A-B}{2}$:

$$\cos x - \cos((2r+1)x) = 2\sin((r+1)x)\sin(rx)$$

So the denominator equals $\sin(rx)\sin((r+1)x)$, giving:

$$f_n(x) = \sum_{r=1}^{n} \frac{\sin^2 x}{\sin(rx)\sin((r+1)x)}$$

## Step 2: Telescoping sum

Using the identity $\cot(rx) - \cot((r+1)x) = \dfrac{\sin x}{\sin(rx)\sin((r+1)x)}$:

$$\frac{\sin^2 x}{\sin(rx)\sin((r+1)x)} = \sin x\bigl(\cot(rx) - \cot((r+1)x)\bigr)$$

Summing telescopically:

$$f_n(x) = \sin x\bigl(\cot x - \cot((n+1)x)\bigr) = \frac{\cos x\sin((n+1)x) - \sin x\cos((n+1)x)}{\sin((n+1)x)} = \frac{\sin(nx)}{\sin((n+1)x)}$$

## Step 3: Compute the product $g_n$

$$g_n(x) = \prod_{r=1}^{n} \frac{\sin(rx)}{\sin((r+1)x)} = \frac{\sin x}{\sin((n+1)x)}$$

(telescoping product — all intermediate terms cancel).

## Step 4: Compute the integrand

$$\frac{f_n(x)}{g_n(x)} = \frac{\sin(nx)/\sin((n+1)x)}{\sin x/\sin((n+1)x)} = \frac{\sin(nx)}{\sin x}$$

So $T_n = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi} \frac{\sin(nx)}{\sin x}\,dx$.

## Step 5: Evaluate $T_n$

Using the standard Fourier expansions:

- **$n$ even** ($n=2m$): $\dfrac{\sin(2mx)}{\sin x} = 2\sum_{j=1}^{m}\cos((2j-1)x)$, and each $\int_0^\pi \cos((2j-1)x)\,dx = 0$, so $T_n = 0$.

- **$n$ odd** ($n=2m+1$): $\dfrac{\sin((2m+1)x)}{\sin x} = 1 + 2\sum_{j=1}^{m}\cos(2jx)$, and each cosine integral vanishes, leaving $T_n = \pi$.

Therefore:
$$T_n = \begin{cases} \pi & n \text{ odd} \\ 0 & n \text{ even} \end{cases}$$

## Step 6: Compute the sum

$$\sum_{r=1}^{10} T_r = \underbrace{T_1+T_3+T_5+T_7+T_9}_{5\text{ odd terms}} + \underbrace{T_2+T_4+T_6+T_8+T_{10}}_{5\text{ even terms}} = 5\pi + 0 = 5\pi$$

Since $\sum_{r=1}^{10} T_r = k\pi$, we obtain:

$$\boxed{k = 5}$$
